Build a REDCap codebook

Source: R/codebook.R
build_codebook.Rd

build_codebook() pulls REDCap project metadata through the API and returns a structured, tidy codebook intended to resemble the information users see in the REDCap UI codebook while remaining useful for downstream R workflows.

Usage

build_codebook(redcap_uri, token)

Arguments

redcap_uri

REDCap API URI.

token

REDCap API token.

Value

A list with classes redcap_codebook and list, containing:

  • fields: one row per field, with display-oriented metadata and configuration summaries.

  • choices: one row per coded choice option.

  • forms: one row per instrument/form.

  • events: one row per REDCap event when the project is longitudinal.

  • event_instruments: one row per event/form mapping when available.

  • repeating: repeating instrument/event configuration when available.

  • project: project-level summary metadata.

  • definitions: a list of complete standardized field/project metadata, source column availability, and a schema version.

The elements other than definitions are tibbles.

Details

Only project metadata is retrieved; records are not exported. Counts describe configured fields, instruments, and events, not populated data. Reuse the returned codebook with view_codebook() or field_relationship_summary() without additional API calls.

Branching logic, calculations, and field annotations are retained as configuration text. The codebook does not evaluate expressions or validate their behavior.

Metadata representation

fields provides selected, display-oriented summaries. definitions$fields and definitions$project retain complete standardized metadata, including additional returned columns, for downstream analysis. Column names and selected flags are normalized; these are not unmodified copies of the API responses.

definitions$source_columns records which standardized columns were actually returned, before missing columns are filled during normalization. This distinguishes an unavailable metadata source from an available but blank one.

field_order follows metadata row order, form_order follows each instrument's first appearance, and choice_order follows the listed option order.

Choices and checkbox exports

choices contains one row per coded option for checkbox, radio, dropdown, Yes/No, and True/False fields. Yes/No and True/False options are supplied implicitly. Calculations are not parsed as choices. Choice codes are retained as character values, including leading zeros.

For checkbox rows in choices (choice_type == "checkbox"), combine field_name and the raw choice_value with three underscores: paste0(field_name, "___", choice_value). This gives the expected raw export column name, such as symptoms___fever. Use the choice code, not its label. field_name remains the parent dictionary field name.

Events and repeating configuration

In fields, event counts and names summarize the events mapped to the field's instrument. Repeating status summarizes instrument-level and event-level repeating configuration across events; it may differ by event. Use event_instruments and repeating for the detailed context rather than treating a field's summary as applying uniformly to every event.

Classic projects have empty event and event-instrument tables. Documented API responses indicating non-applicable configuration produce empty tables; permission and other retrieval failures are reported as errors.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
codebook <- build_codebook(
  redcap_uri = Sys.getenv("REDCAP_URI"),
  token = Sys.getenv("REDCAP_TOKEN")
)

codebook$fields
codebook$choices
} # }
